newsitem.title: USA: Volcano-plagued Montserrat will have pet airlift.
newsitem.headline: Volcano-plagued Montserrat will have pet airlift.

text.p: Dogs and cats from the British island territory Montserrat, plagued for two years by an active volcano, will get a chance for a new life in the United States, a U.S. animal rights group said on Tuesday.
The Boston-based World Society for Protection of Animals said it has arranged to airlift 17 pets next week to Fort Lauderdale, where U.S. families have agreed to take them in.

The animals were left in the southern portion of Montserrat, in an area known as the "danger zone" because scientists said it was most likely to be affected by an eruption of the island's Soufriere Hills volcano.

The southern area, including Montserrat's capital, Plymouth, has been abandoned for much of the last two years, since the volcano roared to life in July 1995. The volcano has remained active since, periodically showering the eastern Caribbean island with ash and rocks.

Residents were forced to abandon pets when they moved to shelters. Others, having lost their livelihoods, can not afford to feed them, the society said. Montserrat's population also has dropped sharply since July 1995. The island now has about 6,800 residents, down from 11,000 two years ago.
"Dogs were tied to abandoned houses and left hungry for at least two weeks at a time," World Society's Field Services Director Gerardo Huertas said.

The group has been providing Montserrat's government with aid for dozens of animals since last year. Its agents have been travelling into the danger zone regularly to feed abandoned animals and it has built a shelter on the island to house animals from the danger zone that cannot be transported to the United States.

A spokeswoman for the society said it was quite easy to bring animals into the United States -- all that is required is a veterinarian's health check and vaccinations -- which has strict policies limiting human immigration.
